title: Stand a glass unit on two setting blocks in a window frame
instruction: Stand the glass unit in the window frame on the two black setting blocks, set on the white marks, and let go. The glass must never touch the sill.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (about 1.6 million in the US, BLS occupation 49-9071) keep buildings in repair, and replacing a broken or misted glazed unit in a window or door is part of that work. On the job the worker takes off the glazing beads, lifts out the failed unit, renews the setting blocks, sets the new unit on them from the room side and pushes it up against the outside stop; the beads go back on after. This task is that setting step. The unit stands on two blocks at its quarter points, so its weight never bears on the sill: glass whose edge comes down on the sill can chip, crack or lose its seal. The head is 6 mm above the standing unit, so it cannot go in from above: its bottom edge goes onto blocks 9 mm above the sill with its top tilted toward the room, then it is turned upright under the head. One arm reaches the blocks, the other the glass. Glass still held, or leaning, is not resting.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. On the table: (1) Frame: a small fixed-light window frame in grey (sRGB 0.60, 0.62, 0.65) aluminium, fixed, standing on the table on the midline with its room side toward the arms: a sill, two jambs and a head, each 60 mm deep (x 27.6 to 33.6 cm) and 20 mm thick, round an opening 240 mm wide (y -12.0 to +12.0 cm) from the sill's top (20 mm above the table) to the head's underside (115 mm above the table). A fixed outside stop runs round the opening on the far side, 15 mm into it, its room-facing face at x 31.3 cm. The room side is open: its glazing bead has been taken off. (2) The bead: a grey (sRGB 0.45, 0.47, 0.50) bar 240 x 12 x 15 mm lying on the table along x to the left of the frame, centred at x 42.0 cm, y +17.0 cm; fixed, a prop. (3) Two quarter-point marks: thin white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.95) plates 30 x 30 x 1 mm fixed on the sill's top, centred at x 29.4 cm, y -5.0 and +5.0 cm. (4) Block tray: a dark grey (sRGB 0.30, 0.30, 0.32) plate 90 x 90 x 4 mm, fixed, centred at x 32.0 cm, y -24.0 cm. (5) Two setting blocks: loose black (sRGB 0.08, 0.08, 0.08) neoprene blocks 30 x 30 x 8 mm, 9 g each, lying flat on the tray, centred at x 30.0 and 34.0 cm, y -24.0 cm. (6) Glass unit: a loose small double-glazed unit (two 2 mm panes on a 20 mm aluminium spacer), 24 mm thick, 200 mm long and 80 mm tall, 0.20 kg, pale blue-grey (sRGB 0.75, 0.85, 0.90), standing on one of its long edges on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm, its length along y and its faces normal to x; for real trials, acrylic panes on a weighted spacer of the same size and mass. Standing on blocks set on the marks against the stop, the unit is 9 mm above the sill, 6 mm below the head and 20 mm from each jamb; the head is over the whole rebate, so the blocks and the unit must go in from the room side. With a top-down grasp only the right arm reaches the blocks and only the left arm reaches the unit: near the table the left arm reaches no further right than about y -10 cm at x 30 cm, short of the blocks at y -22.5 cm, and the right arm no further left than about y +16 cm at x 20 cm, short of the unit's nearer end at y +19 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz): the objects' poses and both arms (TCP, pad tips, gripper opening). 'The opening': from the frame's room face to the outside stop's face (x 27.6 to 31.3 cm), between the jambs (y -12.0 to +12.0 cm). 'Touched the sill': at some step the unit and the sill (any face) or a mark were in contact, touching or pressed into each other: separation 0.0 mm or less, decided exactly for the boxes. Any air gap, however small, is not a touch; that is what a chalk print shows. An object is 'let go' when on each of the last 20 control steps (1 s) both grippers' finger zones (README) were 30 mm or more from it; a step with unreadable arms or an uncomputable distance restarts the count for all. It is 'still' when each of its poses over those 20 steps is within 2 mm and 2 degrees of the current one. 'Standing in the rebate': all eight corners inside the opening from above (1 mm slack), its outside face within 3 mm of the outside stop, tilt under 3 degrees (its height axis from vertical). A block 'lies on the sill' when its 8 mm axis is within 10 degrees of vertical, its lowest point within 1 mm of the sill's or a mark's top and its centre inside the opening. It is 'set' on a mark when it lies on the sill, is let go and still, its sides are within 15 degrees of the opening's and its centre is within 8 mm of the mark's; 'both blocks set': one on each mark. The unit 'rests on' a block only when both are let go and still, the block lies on the sill, at least half of the block's top is under the unit (from above), and the underside is within 1 mm of the block's top there: a held or leaning unit rests on nothing. Score 0 if the unit touched the sill at any moment or at the end is tilted over 30 degrees or off the table. Otherwise: 1.0 if both blocks are set and the unit stands in the rebate resting on both, its centre at most 8 mm off the opening's along y; 0.75 if it stands in the rebate resting on both, the blocks within 20 mm of their marks (one on each, let go and still, sides within 15 degrees) and it is at most 15 mm off centre; 0.5 if it stands in the rebate resting on at least one block; 0.25 if both blocks are set but the unit does not stand in the rebate resting on a block (not brought in, held, leaning, short of the stop); else 0. Read at the last step; the trial ends early (success) once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s. Real trial: blue marking chalk rubbed on the sill (top and room face) and the marks; after the end photo and video the unit is lifted out: any blue on it shows a touch (only contact transfers chalk). A top photo gives block-to-mark distance and turn; ruler and protractor on the end photo the unit's centre and tilt; a 3 mm feeler gauge must not pass between the unit and the stop; the video the 30 mm release and 1 s stillness; resting means standing on its own, let go and still for 1 s.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction, 20 Hz. Simplified: the unit is one uniform box of its stated size and mass; the frame is a small fixed light of plain boxes with a square outside stop; the blocks are rigid. The task ends with the unit set on its blocks against the stop: refitting the glazing bead, the gasket or tape and any sealant are the next steps on the job and not part of it. Not modelled: tape, sealant, breakage, contact forces.
reset_notes: Put the two setting blocks back flat on the tray, centred at x 30.0 and 34.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, their sides along x and y, and the glass unit back standing on a long edge on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm, its faces normal to x. The frame, the marks, the tray and the bead are fixed. Nothing is consumed (in a real build, wipe the unit clean and chalk the sill and marks again).
